findings.title: Meet fallback crashes when no destination calendar is configured
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, but this condition dereferences `.integration` without optional chaining. Creating a Meet event without a configured destination calendar therefore throws before the event or meeting can be created; use a safe check for the missing calendar.

findings.title: Google attendee organizer email always comes from the first destination
findings.body: For each credential, `createEvent` selects that credential's calendar as the event destination, but the organizer attendee email is taken from the first item in the entire destination list. On collective bookings, events created in later hosts' calendars can therefore identify the first host's calendar address as the organizer, misrepresenting who owns the event and potentially breaking organizer-related invite behavior. Select the destination matching `credentialId` for this email too.

findings.title: Google updates lose the destination calendar when no external ID is passed
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this fallback searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that same absent value, so it always yields `undefined`. The update request then receives no calendar ID instead of the event's destination calendar, causing Google updates to fail for callers that omit the external ID. Fall back to the appropriate destination calendar rather than comparing against the missing argument.
